q-111921.name: Question 1
q-111921.worked_solution:
First, notice that all of the terms have a common factor of ${n}^{2}.$ To simplify the computation, we can factor out the ${n}^{2},$ as follows:

$$
9{n}^{4}-{n}^{2}={n}^{2}(9{n}^{2}-1)
$$

Now, we factor the expression $9{n}^{2}-1$ using the difference of squares formula:

$$
{n}^{2}(9{n}^{2}-1)={n}^{2}((3n)^{2}-{1}^{2})={n}^{2}(3n+1)(3n-1)
$$

Question 1
?

Factor the expression 9n4−n2.

a
n2(3n+1)2
b
n2(3n+1)(3n−1)
c
n(3n+1)(3n−1)
d
n2(3n−1)
e
n4(3n−1)
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

First, notice that all of the terms have a common factor of n2. To simplify the computation, we can factor out the n2, as follows:

9n4−n2=n2(9n2−1)

Now, we factor the expression 9n2−1 using the difference of squares formula:

n2(9n2−1)=n2((3n)2−12)=n2(3n+1)(3n−1)

q-111943.name: Question 3
q-111943.worked_solution:
First, notice that all of the terms have a common factor of ${v}^{3}.$ To simplify the computation, we can factor out the ${v}^{3},$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}9{v}^{5}+6{v}^{4}+{v}^{3} & ={v}^{3}(9{v}^{2}+6v+1)\end{aligned}
$$

The expression $9{v}^{2}+6v+1$ is a perfect square trinomial that can be factored as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{v}^{3}(9{v}^{2}+6v+1) & = \\ {v}^{3}((3v)^{2}+6v+{1}^{2}) & = \\ {v}^{3}((3v)^{2}+2\cdot (3v)+{1}^{2}) & = \\ {v}^{3}(3v+1)^{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Question 5
?

The trinomial 4x2z6+8xz6−60z6 is equivalent to

a
4z6(x+3)2
b
4z6(z−6)(z+2)
c
2z6(x−6)(x+5)
d
4z6(x−3)(x+5)
e
4z2(x−3)2
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

Note that all of the terms have a common factor of 4z6. To simplify the computation, we can factor out the 4z6, as follows:

4x2z6+8xz6−60z6=(4z6)⋅x2+(4z6)⋅2x−(4z6)⋅15=4z6(x2+2x−15).

Now, we factor the polynomial x2+2x−15, as follows: 4z6(x2+2x−15)=4z6((x2+5x)+(−3x−15))=4z6(x(x+5)−3(x+5))=4z6(x−3)(x+5)

$$
\begin{aligned}3{x}^{3}+2{x}^{2}-x & =x(3{x}^{2}+2x-1)\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we factor the polynomial $3{x}^{2}+2x-1,$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}x(3{x}^{2}+2x-1) & = \\ x((3{x}^{2}+3x)+(-x-1)) & = \\ x(3x(x+1)-1(x+1)) & = \\ x(3x-1)(x+1)\end{aligned}
$$
